info.title: Stormkit API
info.summary: REST API for the Stormkit deployment platform.
info.description:
The Stormkit API lets you create applications and environments, trigger and publish deployments, read build, runtime and access logs, manage custom domains, redirects, snippets, periodic triggers and transactional email.

Every endpoint is authenticated with an API key sent in the `Authorization` header. Keys are scoped to a user, a team, an application or a single environment; each operation documents the minimum scope it accepts. See https://www.stormkit.io/docs/api/authentication for how to create one.

Stormkit also exposes the same capabilities to agents over MCP at `POST /v1/mcp`; see https://www.stormkit.io/mcp.

get.description: Return this OpenAPI 3.1 document describing every Stormkit API operation. No authentication is required, so an agent can discover the API surface before it holds a key.

paths.description: The available operations, keyed by path.

get.description: Return a paginated list of applications belonging to a team. The page size is fixed at 20; when `hasNextPage` is true, request the next page with `from` increased by the number of apps returned. Requires a team-scoped or user-scoped API key.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: ID of the team to scope results to. The API key owner must be a member.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Pagination offset. Must be zero or greater.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Exact, case-insensitive match on the repository path, e.g. `github/acme/my-app`.

parameters.name: displayName
parameters.description: Exact, case-insensitive match on the application display name.

hasNextPage.description: True when more applications exist beyond this page.

post.description: Create an application, optionally linked to a source-code repository. Omit `repo` to create a bare application that is deployed by uploading a zip file. Requires a team-scoped or user-scoped API key; with a user-scoped key, pass `teamId`.

teamId.description: ID of the team to create the application under. Required with a user-scoped key; ignored with a team-scoped key.

provider.description: Source-code provider. Required when `repo` is a bare `owner/repo` path.

displayName.description: Human-readable application name. Alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores only, with no consecutive hyphens. Generated when omitted.

get.description: Return a single application. With an app-scoped or environment-scoped API key the application is derived from the key; with a broader key, pass `appId`.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application ID. Required unless the API key is already scoped to an application.

get.description: Return a single application addressed by path. Equivalent to `getApp` with the `appId` query parameter.

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: Application ID.

get.summary: Get the published configuration of a host
get.description: Return the build and runtime configuration Stormkit serves for a host name, including the published deployment. Answers 204 when the host has no published deployment.

parameters.name: hostName
parameters.description: Host name to resolve, e.g. `www.example.com`.

configs.description: One entry per deployment serving the host.

items.description: Resolved configuration of a published deployment.

204.description: No published deployment serves this host.

get.description: Return every environment configured for an application, up to 50.

post.description: Create an environment for an application. An environment holds its own branch, build configuration, environment variables and domains.

appId.description: Application to create the environment under.

branch.description: Default git branch deployed for this environment.

put.description: Partially update an environment. Only the fields you send are changed. `envVars` is merged into the existing set: keys you omit keep their value, and a key set to an empty string is removed.

delete.description: Delete an environment together with its deployments, domains and configuration. This cannot be undone.

get.description: Return the decrypted environment variables of an environment. Values are masked everywhere else in the API, so this endpoint is admin-gated and every call is written to the audit log.

200.description: The environment variables, keyed by name.

post.description: Queue a new deployment for an environment and return the created deployment, including its `id`. Poll `getDeployment` until `status` is `success` or `failed`.

appId.description: Application the environment belongs to. Optional when the key is app-scoped.

branch.description: Git branch to deploy. Defaults to the environment's configured branch.

publish.description: Publish the deployment automatically once the build succeeds.

get.description: Return a paginated list of deployments for an environment, newest first. When `hasNextPage` is true, request the next page with `from` increased by the number of deployments returned.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Pagination offset.

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Only return deployments built from this branch.

hasNextPage.description: True when more deployments exist beyond this page.

get.description: Return a single deployment with its status and metadata. Pass `logs=true` to include the build logs.

parameters.name: logs
parameters.description: Include build logs in the response.

delete.description: Delete a deployment and its build artifacts. A published deployment cannot be deleted; publish another one first.

get.description: Return the current status of a deployment in a form cheap enough to poll in a loop. Use it to wait for a build instead of re-reading the whole deployment.

isRunning.description: True while the build is still in progress.

logs.description: Build log entries produced so far.

get.summary: List runtime logs of a deployment
get.description: Return runtime logs — server-side rendering and API function output — produced by a deployment. Paginate with `afterId`/`beforeId`, passing the `id` of the last entry you received.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order by log id.

parameters.name: afterId
parameters.description: Return logs older than this log id. Use together with `sort=desc`.

parameters.name: beforeId
parameters.description: Return logs newer than this log id. Use together with `sort=asc`.

post.description: Make a successfully built deployment live on the environment's domains. Publishing replaces whatever was published before; the previous deployment stays available and can be published again to roll back.
Move a deployment that is still waiting for a build worker to the front of the queue. Deployments already being built cannot be reordered.

200.description: The deployment was moved to the front of the queue.

post.description: Queue a failed deployment for another build with the same commit and configuration. Only deployments whose `status` is `failed` can be restarted.
Cancel a deployment that is queued or currently building.

get.description: Return raw HTTP access logs — one entry per request served — for an environment, newest first. Defaults to the last 24 hours. Paginate by passing `pagination.cursor` from the previous response back verbatim.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only return requests at or after this unix timestamp, in seconds. Defaults to 24 hours ago.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only return requests at or before this unix timestamp, in seconds.

parameters.name: domainId
parameters.description: Only return requests served for this domain.

parameters.name: hostName
parameters.description: Only return requests for this host name.

parameters.name: clientIp
parameters.description: Only return requests from this client IP.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: Only return requests with this HTTP method.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Only return requests whose path starts with this value.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only return requests answered with this HTTP status code.

parameters.name: isBot
parameters.description: Filter bot traffic in or out. Omit to return both.

parameters.name: minDurationMs
parameters.description: Only return requests that took at least this many milliseconds to serve. Requests logged before durations were recorded are excluded.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from the previous response.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many entries to return per page.

200.description: A page of access log entries.

get.description: Return the custom domains attached to an environment, together with their verification state.

parameters.name: domainName
parameters.description: Only return the domain with this exact name.

parameters.name: verified
parameters.description: Only return verified (`true`) or unverified (`false`) domains.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: How many domains to return per page.

parameters.name: afterId
parameters.description: Return domains after this id. Pass `pagination.afterId` from the previous response.

hasNextPage.description: True when more domains exist beyond this page.

afterId.description: Pass this back as `afterId` to fetch the next page.

post.description: Attach a custom domain to an environment. The response contains the verification token to publish as a DNS TXT record before the domain can serve traffic.

envId.description: Environment to attach the domain to.

put.description: Update a custom domain. Use it to re-run verification or to exclude the domain's traffic from analytics.

domainId.description: ID of the domain to update.

analyticsExcluded.description: Exclude requests served for this domain from analytics.

delete.description: Detach a custom domain from an environment. Traffic for that host stops being served immediately.

parameters.name: domainId
parameters.description: ID of the domain to remove. Either this or `id` is required.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Alias of `domainId`.

put.description: Store a custom TLS certificate and private key for a domain instead of letting Stormkit obtain one automatically. Enterprise licence required.

domainId.description: ID of the domain the certificate belongs to.

certKey.description: PEM-encoded private key. Write-only; never returned.

delete.description: Delete the custom certificate of a domain. Stormkit falls back to automatically issued certificates. Enterprise licence required.

parameters.name: domainId
parameters.description: ID of the domain whose certificate is removed. Either this or `id` is required.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Alias of `domainId`.

get.description: Return the redirect and rewrite rules configured for an environment, in the order they are evaluated.

post.description: Replace the environment's redirect and rewrite rules with the list you send. Rules are evaluated top to bottom and the first match wins.

redirects.description: The complete set of rules. An empty array removes every rule.

get.description: Return the code snippets injected into HTML served by an environment.

parameters.name: hosts
parameters.description: Comma-separated host names. Only snippets whose rules match one of them are returned.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Only return snippets with this title.

parameters.name: afterId
parameters.description: Return snippets after this id. Pass `pagination.afterId` from the previous response.

hasNextPage.description: True when more snippets exist beyond this page.

afterId.description: Pass this back as `afterId` to fetch the next page.

post.description: Add one or more snippets that Stormkit injects into the `head` or `body` of HTML responses, optionally limited to matching hosts and paths.

envId.description: Environment to add the snippets to.

put.description: Update an existing snippet. Send the complete snippet, including its `id`; the stored snippet is replaced by what you send.

delete.description: Remove one or more snippets from an environment. They stop being injected on the next request.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated snippet ids to delete, e.g. `1501,5061`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A single snippet id to delete. Takes precedence over `ids`.

get.description: Return the periodic (cron) triggers configured for an environment.

post.description: Create a trigger that sends an HTTP request to a URL on a cron schedule, evaluated in UTC.

envId.description: Environment to attach the trigger to.

cron.description: Cron expression evaluated in UTC, e.g. `*/5 * * * *`.

patch.description: Partially update a trigger: only the fields you send are changed. To clear a field, send its empty value explicitly.

triggerId.description: ID of the trigger to update.

delete.description: Delete a trigger. Scheduled runs stop immediately; recorded execution logs are removed with it.

parameters.name: triggerId
parameters.description: ID of the trigger to delete.

post.description: Run a trigger immediately, regardless of its schedule or status. The call is synchronous and returns the execution log, which is also stored alongside the scheduled runs.

triggerId.description: ID of the trigger to run.

200.description: The execution log of the run.

get.description: Return the last 25 executions of a trigger — scheduled and manual — most recent first.

parameters.name: triggerId
parameters.description: ID of the trigger to read logs for.

post.description: Send a transactional email through the environment's SMTP configuration. An environment without a mailer still records the email without sending it, so check `delivered`, not only `ok`.

to.description: Recipient address. Separate multiple recipients with a semicolon.

from.description: Sender address. Defaults to the SMTP username when empty.

ok.description: True when the request was accepted and recorded.

delivered.description: False when the environment has no SMTP configuration, so nothing was handed to a mail server.

get.description: Return the SMTP configuration of an environment. The password is never returned: when one is stored, `password` holds the placeholder `****-****-****-****`; when no mailer is configured, `config` is null.

config.description: The stored configuration, or null when the environment has no mailer.

post.description: Update the SMTP configuration of an environment. Only the fields you send are changed. `password` is write-only: omit it to keep the stored one. Changing `smtpHost` or `username` clears the stored password, so those calls must carry a new one.

smtpPort.description: SMTP server port. Defaults to 587 when empty.

username.description: SMTP username, usually the sending address.

password.description: SMTP password. Write-only and never returned.

200.description: The stored configuration, with the password masked.

get.description: Return the last 100 emails recorded for an environment, newest first. Message bodies are never included and recipient addresses are masked, because the log holds magic-link emails and the app's end-user mailing list.

post.description: Upload one or more files to the environment's persistent volume. Files survive deployments and are served from the mounted volume path.

envId.description: Environment whose volume is written to.

413.description: The upload exceeded the maximum allowed request body size.

get.description: Return every team the API key owner belongs to. Community edition returns only the default team. Requires a user-scoped API key.

200.description: The teams of the key owner.

post.description: Create a team owned by the API key owner. Enterprise licence required.

JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint implementing the Model Context Protocol. Use `initialize`, `tools/list` and `tools/call` to drive Stormkit from an agent. The same operations documented here are exposed as MCP tools. Requires a user-scoped API key.

id.description: Request id echoed back in the response.
The id of the request this responds to.

result.description: Method result. Present when the call succeeded.

error.description: JSON-RPC error. Present when the call failed.

get.description: Server-sent events stream used by MCP clients that negotiate the streamable HTTP transport. Requires a user-scoped API key.

schema.description: Server-sent event stream of JSON-RPC messages.

get.description: Return the end-user authentication configuration of an environment: session settings, allowed origins and OAuth-server settings. Secrets are never included. Available on self-hosted instances.

post.description: Update end-user authentication for an environment. Only the fields you send are changed. Available on self-hosted instances.

get.description: Return the configured Stormkit Auth sign-in providers of an environment. Client secrets are never returned. Available on self-hosted instances.

post.description: Enable or update a single sign-in provider. `magiclink` needs `fromAddress` and a configured mailer; `google` and `x` need `clientId` and `clientSecret`. Client secrets are write-only. Requires the database integration. Available on self-hosted instances.

status.description: Whether the provider is enabled. Omit to keep the current value.

fromAddress.description: Sender address for magic-link emails. Required for `magiclink`.

clientId.description: OAuth client ID. Required for OAuth providers.

clientSecret.description: OAuth client secret. Write-only; omit to keep the stored one.

get.description: Return the managed Postgres schema attached to an environment, including the connection details injected into the application. Available on self-hosted instances.

200.description: The database integration of the environment.

post.description: Create the managed Postgres schema of an environment and store the generated credentials on it. The schema name is derived from the application and environment.

200.description: The credentials of the created schema.

409.description: The environment already has a schema.

delete.description: Detach the managed Postgres schema from an environment. Available on self-hosted instances.

post.description: Control how the environment's managed schema is wired into the application: whether its connection details are injected as environment variables, and whether migrations run on deploy.

injectEnvVars.description: Inject the schema's connection details as environment variables.

migrationsEnabled.description: Run migrations from the repository on every deployment.

migrationsFolder.description: Folder holding the migration files, relative to the repository root.

ApiKeyAuth.name: Authorization
ApiKeyAuth.description: A Stormkit API key, sent verbatim (no `Bearer` prefix). Keys are scoped to a user, a team, an application or a single environment. Create one in the dashboard: https://www.stormkit.io/docs/api/authentication

EnvIdQueryOptional.name: envId
EnvIdQueryOptional.description: Environment ID. Required unless the API key is already scoped to an environment.

AppIdQueryOptional.name: appId
AppIdQueryOptional.description: Application ID. Required unless the API key is already scoped to an application.

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed or a parameter failed validation.

example.error: Authentication is required. Send your Stormkit API key in the Authorization header.

Forbidden.description: The API key is missing, invalid, or its scope is too narrow for this operation.

example.error: The API key is missing, invalid, or does not grant access to this resource.

NotFound.description: The addressed resource does not exist or is not visible to this API key.

example.error: The requested resource was not found.

InternalError.description: The request failed unexpectedly. Retry later; if it persists, contact support.

Error.description: Structured error payload returned by every failing API call.

error.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable error code, e.g. `forbidden` or `not-found`.

docs.description: Documentation page explaining how to resolve this class of error.

errors.description: Field-level validation messages, keyed by field name. Present on validation failures.

Ok.description: Acknowledgement returned by operations that have no payload of their own.

hasNextPage.description: True when more entries exist beyond this page.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor. Pass it back verbatim to fetch the next page.

id.description: Unique application ID. Use it as `appId` elsewhere.

repo.description: Repository path, e.g. `github/acme/my-app`. Empty when `isBare` is true.

isBare.description: True when no repository is linked and deployments are uploaded as zip files.

userId.description: ID of the user who owns the application.

teamId.description: ID of the team the application belongs to.

defaultEnvId.description: ID of the default environment. Use it as `envId` elsewhere.

createdAt.description: Unix timestamp, in seconds, of when the application was created.

EnvironmentSettings.description: Build and runtime settings shared by environment create and update.

workDir.description: Working directory, relative to the repository root, where install and build run.

serverCmd.description: Command that starts the server process. Self-hosted only.

apiFolder.description: Path to the API / serverless functions folder.

apiPathPrefix.description: URL prefix routed to API functions. Defaults to `/api`.

errorFile.description: Custom error page served instead of `404.html`.

headers.description: Custom response headers in Netlify / Caddy format.

headersFile.description: Path to a headers file, relative to the repository root.

redirectsFile.description: Path to a redirects file, relative to the repository root.

autoDeploy.description: Deploy automatically on every push to the configured branch.

autoDeployBranches.description: Comma-separated branch patterns that trigger auto-deploy.

autoDeployCommits.description: Regular expression matched against commit messages to trigger auto-deploy.

previewLinks.description: Generate a preview link for each deployment.

priorityPattern.description: Regular expression matched against commit messages; matching auto-deploys go to the priority queue.

envVars.description: Environment variables injected at build and run time.

statusChecks.description: Commands run after a successful deployment to verify it.

cacheDirs.description: Directories restored before install and snapshotted after a successful build, e.g. `.next/cache`. Pass an empty array to disable caching.

Environment.description: An environment of an application: its branch, build configuration and URLs.

id.description: Environment ID. Use it as `envId` elsewhere.

appId.description: ID of the application the environment belongs to.

branch.description: Git branch deployed for this environment.

preview.description: URL where the published deployment of this environment is served.

published.description: Currently published deployments and their traffic share.

percentage.description: Share of traffic served by this deployment.

build.description: Resolved build configuration of the environment.

lastDeploy.description: Summary of the most recent deployment.

Deployment.description: A single build of an environment.

isRunning.description: True while the build is in progress.

isPublished.description: True when this deployment currently serves traffic.

percentage.description: Share of traffic served by this deployment.

preview.description: Preview URL of this specific deployment.

logs.description: Build log entries. Included when requested.

createdAt.description: Unix timestamp, in seconds, of when the deployment was created.

stoppedAt.description: Unix timestamp, in seconds, of when the build finished.

Domain.description: A custom domain attached to an environment.

verified.description: True once the DNS TXT record has been verified.

token.description: Verification token to publish as a DNS TXT record.

customCert.description: True when a custom TLS certificate is stored for this domain.

lastPing.description: Result of the most recent reachability check.

analyticsExcluded.description: True when requests for this domain are excluded from analytics.

status.description: HTTP status code to answer with. Omit for a rewrite.

assets.description: Apply the rule to asset requests as well.

hosts.description: Only apply the rule to these host names.

headers.description: Extra response headers set when the rule matches.

prepend.description: Inject as the first child of the location instead of the last.

interpolate.description: Interpolate system variables such as `{{SK_REQUEST_ID}}` at request time. Unflagged snippets are injected verbatim.

rules.description: Conditions restricting where the snippet is injected.

hosts.description: Only inject on these host names.

path.description: Only inject on paths matching this regular expression.

TriggerInput.description: Writable fields of a periodic trigger.

status.description: Whether the trigger is active. Inactive triggers are not scheduled.

description.description: One-line summary shown next to the trigger. Maximum 200 characters.

documentation.description: Markdown notes about the trigger. Displayed in the dashboard only.

method.description: HTTP method used for the request. Defaults to GET.

payload.description: Request body, sent for non-GET methods.

nextRunAt.description: Unix timestamp, in seconds, of the next scheduled run.

TriggerLog.description: One execution of a periodic trigger.

status.description: HTTP status code returned by the called URL.

response.description: Response body captured from the call, truncated.

createdAt.description: Unix timestamp, in seconds, of the execution.

MailerConfig.description: SMTP configuration of an environment. The password is never returned.

password.description: Always the placeholder `****-****-****-****` when a password is stored.

Email.description: An email recorded by the mailer. Bodies are never stored in the log and recipients are masked.

delivered.description: True when the message was handed to an SMTP server.

createdAt.description: Unix timestamp, in seconds, of when the email was recorded.

AccessLog.description: One HTTP request served by an environment.

ts.description: Unix timestamp, in seconds, of when the request was served.

hostName.description: Host name the request was served for.

domainId.description: ID of the matching custom domain, when any.

isBot.description: True when the request was classified as bot traffic.

durationMs.description: How long the request took to serve, in milliseconds.

RuntimeLog.description: One runtime log line produced by server-side rendering or an API function.

id.description: Log entry ID. Use it as `afterId`/`beforeId` to paginate.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp, in seconds, of when the line was produced.

id.description: Team ID. Use it as `teamId` elsewhere.

isDefault.description: True for the personal team created with the account.

currentUserRole.description: Role of the API key owner in this team, e.g. `owner`, `admin` or `developer`.

AuthConfig.description: Stormkit Auth configuration of an environment. Secrets are never returned.

allowedOrigins.description: Origins allowed to start a sign-in flow.

oauthServer.description: Settings of the built-in OAuth authorization server.

AuthProvider.description: A configured sign-in provider. Client secrets are never returned.

clientId.description: OAuth client ID, for OAuth providers.

fromAddress.description: Sender address used for magic-link emails.

DatabaseSchema.description: The managed Postgres schema attached to an environment.
